articles.title: Sharp cold snap to follow weekend warmth in the Midwest and Northeast
articles.summary: The East stays mild into the weekend, but a cold front crossing the Midwest Sunday opens the door to Canadian air early next week. Morning lows in parts of Pennsylvania and New York could be 15 to 25 degrees colder Wednesday than Monday. Lake-effect snow showers may slick roads near Cleveland and Erie, though no widespread heavy snow is expected.

articles.title: Wind, rain and storms to bump early Thanksgiving trips in the Plains and Midwest
articles.summary: A storm system brings gusts near 40 mph to southern Minnesota and Missouri Friday, plus rain in the Twin Cities. On Saturday, showers and storms spread across the Plains, and a few near Oklahoma City or Kansas City could bring hail. Colder air follows Sunday, though travel delays should stay limited this weekend.

articles.title: Florida flooding forces over 100 rescues as storm eyes East Coast
articles.summary: Days of torrential rain flooded Florida's Atlantic coast, and more than 100 people were rescued in Brevard County on Thursday. Hollywood got over a foot of rain in hours. The storm, which has a medium chance of becoming Kyle, is expected to move up the East Coast Sunday into Monday.

articles.title: El Niño could make December one of the warmest on record in the U.S.
articles.summary: Forecasters expect most of the country to run warmer than a typical December, with the strongest warm signal in the Midwest, Great Lakes and interior Northeast. California and much of the Southeast may turn out wetter than usual.

articles.title: San Francisco sets a rain record as third atmospheric river hits California
articles.summary: San Francisco got 2.31 inches of rain Wednesday, a daily record dating to 1918, as flooding spread across the Bay Area. Gusts topped 50 mph near Sacramento and Modesto, and heavy Sierra snow shut I-80 at Donner Pass.

articles.title: Weekend East Coast storm could become Subtropical Storm Kyle
articles.summary: A low expected to form off Florida by Friday may bring rain, wind and coastal flooding from northeast Florida to Virginia this weekend, then reach the Northeast Sunday into Monday. It could earn the name Kyle, and flight delays are possible at Northeast hubs Monday.

articles.title: Rare waterspouts and tornado warnings hit the Bay Area as storms roll in
articles.summary: Two waterspouts spun up over San Francisco Bay near Candlestick Point and Brisbane, something NOAA records show hasn't happened there in 28 years. No damage was reported. Santa Cruz County also saw two tornado warnings without a confirmed tornado, and Wednesday's storm could drop 1 to 2 inches of rain.

articles.title: Record-setting super El Niño comes as Atlantic logs just one hurricane
articles.summary: Parts of the eastern tropical Pacific are running up to 18°F warmer than normal, and by many measures this is the strongest super El Niño yet seen. The Atlantic has produced only one hurricane this season, a first since 1925. Waters off California are also near record warmth.

articles.title: Next atmospheric river puts 30 million Californians at risk of flash flooding
articles.summary: Another atmospheric river reaches California Tuesday night, bringing a flash flood threat to more than 30 million people through Thursday. The Bay Area could get 2 to 3 inches of rain Wednesday, then heavy rain shifts to Los Angeles Thursday, where burn scars face debris flow risk. The highest Sierra peaks could see over 4 feet of snow.

articles.title: Rain and mountain snow could slow weekend travel in the West and Plains
articles.summary: This weekend, Nov. 20-22, a storm could spread snow from the Four Corners toward the Northern Plains, while a new system brings rain and mountain snow from San Francisco to Seattle. Showers linger in Florida and along the Southeast coast, and storms may reach the I-95 corridor Sunday. Thanksgiving week looks warmer than average for most of the country.

articles.title: Sunny, unusually mild days ahead for much of the eastern U.S.
articles.summary: High pressure will keep much of the East dry and sunny this week, with highs 5 to 15 degrees above average. New York and Chicago could reach the mid-60s Thursday and Friday, and Nashville, Atlanta and Charlotte may near 70. The dry stretch could raise wildfire risk in drought areas.

articles.title: Florida's Atlantic coast faces a week of flooding rain, with Brevard most at risk
articles.summary: Repeated downpours are set to soak Florida's east coast from Tuesday through Friday, with 4 to 6 inches widely and over 8 inches in spots. Parts of Brevard County face a Level 3 of 4 flash flood risk Wednesday. Forecasters say the storms could turn into a coastal storm by Saturday, bringing wind and rain to the Southeast.

articles.title: Florida's Atlantic coast braces for days of heavy rain bands
articles.summary: Easterly winds off the Atlantic could push repeated bands of heavy rain into Central Florida from Tuesday through Friday. Most areas may see 2 to 4 inches, with 5 to 7 possible in spots, and flooding is most likely south of Cape Canaveral midweek. The St. Johns River is already in major flood at Cocoa.

articles.title: Big surf pounds Southern California beaches and closes piers
articles.summary: Waves of 6 to 9 feet were forecast in spots like Ventura's Surfers Point on Sunday, and piers in Manhattan Beach, Huntington Beach, Ventura and San Diego's Pacific Beach closed at times. Waves washed away a protective berm in Seal Beach. Dangerous rip currents may last all week as rain chances return Monday.

articles.title: Early Thanksgiving outlook: warm North, cooler and stormier South
articles.summary: A storm could bring rain from the Mississippi and Ohio valleys to the East Coast early in Thanksgiving week, then move offshore before the holiday. The Northeast and Great Lakes look unusually warm, while the Southwest and southern Plains run cooler. Severe storms are possible in Texas and the Gulf Coast over the holiday weekend.

articles.title: Super El Niño could mean a snowier winter for the Mountain West
articles.summary: After record-low snowpack last winter, NOAA and European outlooks favor above-average snow from November to March for the Sierra Nevada, Great Basin, Wasatch and central Rockies. The Cascades may come in below average. That mountain snow is a key water source for the Colorado River and the Southwest.

articles.title: Nashville in for a sunny but chilly weekend, with frost possible tonight
articles.summary: Middle Tennessee will run about 7 to 10 degrees below average this weekend, with a high near 52 on Saturday. A low around 29 could bring patchy frost and freezing temps by Sunday morning, so cover sensitive plants. Readings should get closer to normal next week.

articles.title: Mid-South drought eases in spots but keeps spreading in eastern Arkansas
articles.summary: Memphis has picked up 3.41 inches of rain this month, more than August through October combined, yet it is still about an inch below normal for November. Most of West Tennessee and north Mississippi improved to moderate or severe drought, while eastern Arkansas keeps getting worse. Little rain is expected until a front around Thanksgiving week.

articles.title: Record-early polar vortex disruption could bring more cold around Thanksgiving
articles.summary: The earliest polar vortex disruption on record pushed Arctic air into the eastern U.S. this week, helping this week's nor'easter drop snow in higher areas. Forecast models hint at another round of cold, and possibly snow, in the East around Thanksgiving weekend.

articles.title: Weekend storm brings a long-awaited soaking to Texas
articles.summary: The storm that brought rain and mountain snow to California is crossing Texas and Oklahoma into early next week. Dallas has had just 0.19 inch of rain since Oct. 5, so the downpours should mostly help. Houston, Austin and San Antonio also get storms, and flash flooding is possible in central and coastal Texas.

articles.title: Nor'easter soaks the I-95 corridor as the season's first snow falls up north
articles.summary: A nor'easter brought heavy rain and wind to the East Coast on Friday. The heaviest snow was expected Friday afternoon into Saturday morning in upstate New York, southern Vermont and New Hampshire, with 1 to 3 inches possible in the Adirondacks and the Green and White Mountains. Lake-effect rain and snow were set to follow around the Great Lakes.

articles.title: Storm train hits the West with Sierra snow, strong winds and huge surf
articles.summary: A string of storms is moving across the West, with up to 2 feet of snow possible on the highest Sierra Nevada peaks near Lake Tahoe and Mammoth Lakes. A high surf warning from Monterey to Crescent City calls for waves as high as 35 feet on Saturday, and another storm could arrive Wednesday.

articles.title: Boston gets mostly cold rain as the nor'easter moves out
articles.summary: Greater Boston saw mainly a cold rain from Friday's nor'easter, with north-northeast winds gusting to around 30 mph. Some higher spots in New England picked up a few inches of snow before the storm pulled away.

articles.title: This El Niño may soon become the strongest on record
articles.summary: Pacific waters in NOAA's key monitoring zone were 2.5°C above average in mid-November, and NOAA puts the odds of a historic event at about 60%. Its effects have already shown up, including the fewest Atlantic hurricanes since 1925. A warm North, wet South pattern is expected through at least February.
